newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles down after contract lows.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles down after contract lows.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures continued recent losses Wednesday after a number of contracts posted new life-of-contract lows on growing bearish sentiment over power demand and supplies in the western U.S.
"All the people are bearish on the market with all the hydro," said a Houston futures trader.
Reports of snowpack climbing toward record levels in the Northwest and strong runoffs after recent storms in northern California are contributing to the bearish mood, market sources said.
March California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 30 cents at $11.10 a megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract low of $10.90.
April COB finished down 50 cents at $10.00 after setting a new contract low at $9.75. Other active contracts ended 25 to 45 cents lower.
March Palo Verde (PV) settled down 20 cents at $13.40 after bouncing between $13.25 and $13.40.
April PV finished down 15 cents at $12.35 after posting a contract low of $12.25. Active deferred PV months ended 30 to 60 cents lower.

In addition to plenty of hydroelectric supplies, forecasts of mild weather in the West also pressured cash prices lower. Firm, peak day-ahead power at COB and PV fell 50 cents to $1 from Tuesday's quotes.
The Northwest is forecast to experience mild and very wet weather through the end of the week, while the Southwest is expected to stay warm and dry during the same period.
February gas deliveries to the San Juan Hub in New Mexico softened to $2.41-$2.45 per million British thermal units from Tuesday's $2.42-$2.46.
NYMEX March Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 10.8 cents at $2.438.
Barring a technical recovery or revised forecasts of a deep freeze in the West, the complex is expected to continue its downward trend, market sources.
"You're at a level where you're not comfortable either way," said the Houston trader.
Transmission on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie will be reduced on Saturday as well as Monday through Wednesday next week for maintenance.

Restart of a 500 kilovolt transmission line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to the Canadian border, was delayed toward the end of the week after damage from an ice storm almost two weeks ago.
A 262 megawatt coal-fired unit at the Rawhide power plant in northern Colorado began startup today after being shut last Saturday for boiler tube repairs.
NYMEX estimated 220 COB and 50 PV contracts were sold, well below Tuesday's levels.
